Parse JSON into R objects (jsonlite's fromJSON, natively)

Source: R/json_native.R
fromjs.Rd

Reads JSON text, a JSON file or a JSON address on the web into R objects, with the same simplification rules as jsonlite's fromJSON(): an array of numbers becomes a numeric vector, an array of records a data frame, an array of equal-length arrays a matrix. The parser is this package's own, so it works without jsonlite, and it is stricter in two places that matter for provenance records: a repeated key is an error by default, and a whole number too large for a double is flagged.

Usage

fromjs(
  txt,
  simplifyVector = TRUE,
  simplifyDataFrame = simplifyVector,
  simplifyMatrix = simplifyVector,
  flatten = FALSE,
  bigint_as_char = FALSE,
  simplify = NULL,
  duplicate_keys = c("error", "keep"),
  bigint_warn = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

txt

JSON text (a character vector, joined with newlines), a file path, an http(s) URL, or a connection. A URL goes through the same check and the same transport as every other fetch in the package (public https host, redirects re-checked, body capped).

simplifyVector

Logical scalar, default TRUE: turn arrays of scalars into atomic vectors.

simplifyDataFrame

Logical scalar, default simplifyVector: turn arrays of records into data frames.

simplifyMatrix

Logical scalar, default simplifyVector: turn arrays of equal-length arrays into matrices.

flatten

Logical scalar, default FALSE. TRUE expands nested data frame columns into columns named outer.inner.

bigint_as_char

Logical scalar, default FALSE: integers beyond 2^53 come back as strings.

simplify

Legacy, default NULL: FALSE turns every simplification off.

duplicate_keys

What to do with an object that repeats a key: "error" (default) refuses the document, "keep" returns both values under the repeated name, as jsonlite does.

bigint_warn

Logical scalar, default TRUE: warn (once per document) when a whole number beyond 2^53 is read into a double; the package's own readers of API payloads turn this off, since long numeric identifiers are routine there.

...

Ignored, for call compatibility with jsonlite.

Value

An R object: a list, an atomic vector, a data frame, a matrix or NULL, depending on the JSON and the simplification options.

Details

A single string shorter than 2,084 bytes that is not valid JSON is taken as a location: an http(s) address is fetched (a public https host only, redirects re-checked, 60 second timeout, body capped at 16 MiB), otherwise an existing file is read. Anything else is parsed as JSON text; a character vector is joined with newlines. A connection is read to its end (and closed when this call opened it).

Without simplification (simplifyVector = FALSE) objects become named lists, arrays unnamed lists, null NULL, and numbers integer or double. Whole numbers beyond \(2^{53}\) cannot be held exactly in a double: they are read as doubles with a warning, or kept as text with bigint_as_char = TRUE.

Errors: txt not character or a connection; invalid JSON (the message gives the character offset); a repeated key under duplicate_keys = "error"; an address that is not a public https host, that cannot be reached or that answers with an HTTP error.

See also

tojs() for the reverse.

Examples

fromjs('[{"a":1,"b":"x"},{"a":2,"b":"y"}]')
#>   a b
#> 1 1 x
#> 2 2 y
fromjs('[[1,2],[3,4]]')
#>      [,1] [,2]
#> [1,]    1    2
#> [2,]    3    4

# no simplification: nested lists exactly as in the document
str(fromjs('{"a": [1, 2], "b": {"c": null}}', simplifyVector = FALSE))
#> List of 2
#>  $ a:List of 2
#>   ..$ : int 1
#>   ..$ : int 2
#>  $ b:List of 1
#>   ..$ c: NULL

# from a file
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
writeLines('[{"a":1},{"a":2,"b":"x"}]', f)
fromjs(f)
#>   a    b
#> 1 1 <NA>
#> 2 2    x

# a large identifier kept exactly, as text
fromjs('[12345678901234567890]', bigint_as_char = TRUE)
#> [1] "12345678901234567890"

# a repeated key is refused unless asked for
try(fromjs('{"a": 1, "a": 2}'))
#> Error : duplicate key "a" at character 17
fromjs('{"a": 1, "a": 2}', duplicate_keys = "keep")
#> $a
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $a
#> [1] 2
#>
